argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0210b: meeting "b" (functional design) of series SY0210.

PROJECT
The team is designing a voice-controlled kitchen timer.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Project Manager (PM)  Rachel  present
B  Marketing Expert (ME)  Tom  present
C  User Interface designer (UI)  Priya  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Marcus  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0210a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting for a voice-controlled kitchen timer and introduced the team, noting that the user interface designer was absent. She presented the project aim and budget: a selling price of 25 euros, a maximum production cost of 12.50 euros per unit including all components, and an overall profit target of 50 million euros. The team discussed initial requirements, including kitchen background noise as a challenge for voice recognition, the need for a manual backup control, the target market, and the open question of battery versus mains power. A planned new survey of home cooks was dropped after the marketing expert pointed out that last year's company kitchen appliance survey already covers timers and cooking habits; he will extract the relevant data instead. The user interface designer was given the voice command and spoken feedback work in her absence, and the next meeting will be the functional design meeting.
  decisions: The timer will have at least one physical button as a backup to voice control. The target market is home cooks rather than professional kitchens. The new survey of home cooks will not be carried out; existing survey data from last year will be used instead.
  actions: The marketing expert will extract the timer and cooking-habit findings from last year's kitchen appliance survey for the next meeting. The industrial designer will research microphones, speech recognition chips and power options, with rough costs. The user interface designer (absent) will work out the voice command list and how the timer responds to the user. The user interface designer (absent) will also look at the idea of named, multiple simultaneous timers. The project manager will email the user interface designer with her tasks and the meeting notes, and will circulate the minutes.
  problems: Kitchen background noise may stop the timer from hearing commands, and using more than one microphone would add cost within a tight 12.50 euro budget. Whether the timer runs on batteries or plugs in is unresolved: always-on listening drains batteries, while a cable is unpopular on counters. The industrial designer's suggestion of a magnetic back for mounting on a fridge or cooker hood was not agreed and was deferred to the conceptual design meeting. The marketing expert's idea of named, multiple simultaneous timers was not decided and was passed to the user interface designer.
  action item SY0210a.ai1: Run a new survey of about fifty home cooks on what they want from a voice-controlled timer (owner B, dropped)
  action item SY0210a.ai2: Extract the timer and cooking-habit findings from last year's kitchen appliance (kettle line) survey for the next meeting (owner B, active)
  action item SY0210a.ai3: Research microphones, speech recognition chips and power options (battery vs plug-in), with rough costs (owner D, active)
  action item SY0210a.ai4: Work out the voice command list and how the timer answers back to the user, for the next meeting (owner C, active)
  action item SY0210a.ai5: Look at the idea of named, multiple simultaneous timers (e.g. 'pasta timer') (owner C, active)
  action item SY0210a.ai6: Email the user interface designer her tasks and the meeting notes (owner A, active)
  action item SY0210a.ai7: Send the meeting minutes round to the team (owner A, active)
  fact (absence): The user interface designer, Priya (C), was absent from the kickoff meeting because she was off sick.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer proposed a magnetic back for sticking the timer to a fridge or cooker hood; the marketing expert had doubts, and it was deferred to the conceptual design meeting.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert proposed named, multiple simultaneous timers; it was not adopted and was passed to the user interface designer to look at.
  fact (action_item_removed): The marketing expert's task to run a new survey of about fifty home cooks was dropped.
  fact (plan_change): Instead of running a new survey, the team will reuse last year's company kitchen appliance survey (about two thousand responses), which covers timers and cooking habits.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F2_VAGUE_NO_OWNER [F2]: A task is mentioned vaguely ("someone should probably check the costs") and no one takes it. The gold action item has owner null and owner_unclear true.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.
- F2_OFFERED_TAKEN_BY_OTHER [F2]: One person offers to do a task ("I could look into ..."), but a different person ends up taking it. The gold owner is the person who took it, and the history records the offer and the acceptance.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
